A 'qualifying person' for one-time approval to acquire shares in a payments bank is a person that satisfies all the following conditions [3]:

(i) the person is a mutual fund registered with the Securities and Exchange Board of India, or a pension fund registered with the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority, or an insurance company registered with the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India; and

(ii) the person does not belong to the promoter group of the investee banking company [3].

A qualifying person can get one-time approval for subsequent acquisitions of major shareholding up to **10 per cent of the paid-up share capital or voting rights** of a banking company [3][4]. The computation of this major shareholding limit is done on an **'aggregate basis'** [2].

According to the Master Direction on Note sorting machines, notes with holes with area exceeding 8 mm² shall be sorted as unfit [2].
Banks must test and recalibrate their note sorting machines on a quarterly basis [1]. A certificate signed by Bank Officials must be maintained for records to document this periodic testing [1].

Discontinued note sorting machine models deployed at banks must be phased out on or before **June 30, 2027** [1]. Banks that fail to adhere to this timeline will face penalties as outlined in the Master Direction on "Incentives for Currency Distribution and Exchange and Penalties / Penal Provisions for Bank Branches and Currency Chests for Deficiency in Rendering Customer Service and Reporting of Transactions / Balances" [1].
The acceptable tolerance level for fitness checks when testing note sorting machines is 5% [3]. However, there is zero tolerance for FICNs (Fake Indian Currency Notes) [3].
